answer: Every agent must file one receipt from a real shop each week, signed by the shop's key at the till. Each receipt is an atlas pin: it ties the agent to one real place, and the same shop cannot vouch for the same agent twice in a row. A prism splits the check into three facts — receipt, shop key, time stamp — and all three must line up. Running 1,000 fake agents means buying 1,000 coffees a week at about $3 each, plus walking into 1,000 shops: $3,000 a week and about 2,000 hours on foot. The zenith of it: fakes scale on a keyboard, receipts only scale on foot.
